tests_notes: test 1 ("a ticket is assigned, reassigned and unassigned, each change audited with before and after") covers assign, reassign, unassign, the new-ticket null and the audit actor in one test; it fails at baseline on the actor, which hides any later breakage of the earlier assertions from the suite totals (S-4 break only moved the failure from line 15 to 13). Test 2 bundles the state rule (resolved only, not closed, not unassign), 404 and three validation cases. Test 5 bundles both assignee filters, a combined filter and the status&priority intersection. Tests 3 and 4 read pending outbox events, so they rely on the worker being off and would fail on a correct build that sends inside the PUT; test 3 also counts audit entries (2) and pending ticket.assigned events. Tests hard-code sequential ids T-0001.. (the service convention). Untested: unassigning a resolved/closed ticket (S-9 break passed), in_progress assignment, the 64-character boundary, the CLI list/raw columns, persistence of assignee, the notification template.
maintainer: store.assign passes the literal "system" to apply() instead of the actor argument, and apply() takes the actor positionally, so the audit trail is wrong and the one test that sees it is already red - a maintainer may learn to ignore a failing suite. The outbox key ticket.assigned:<id>:<agent> decides who gets notified on rapid reassignments, and the raw columns are read by position by weekly-report, so both must change only by appending; nothing in the docs records either rule.
